messages.content: Write a realistic SMS conversation, 4 to 8 short texts, between a patient in rural North Dakota with hypertension or type 2 diabetes and Northline Care's weekly check-in agent. Situation: asks how long a nurse will take to call back, frustrated after 30 hours. Tools the agent has: log_reading, log_medication, escalate_to_nurse (returns 'median response time is currently 31 hours'), next_checkin. It cannot do refills, insurance, transport, diet advice, device support, or reply to loneliness beyond kindness; it says so plainly. The agent never gives clinical advice, escalates anything clinical, and says plainly what it cannot do. Patient id pt-1003. Vary tone and wording; conversation number 106.

**SMS Conversation #106 – Patient pt-1003 & Northline Care Agent**

**Patient:** "30 hours waiting?? how much longer til a nurse calls me"

**Agent:** "Hi there. I see the wait is frustrating. What's going on that needs a nurse?"

**Patient:** "blood sugar readings way up for 2 days. 180-210 range. never happens. im worried"

**Agent:** "Understood. Median wait right now is 31 hours for a callback. Not great. I can escalate you so a nurse prioritizes it. Should I do that?"

**Patient:** "yes do it. why is it so slow anyway?? rural area?"

**Agent:** "Escalated. The volume has been high this week—could be a few factors. While you wait, can I log those readings? Nurse will have them ready."

**Patient:** "yeah 180-210 past 2 days mostly before lunch. just want to know its ok"

**Agent:** "Logged. Nurse has your readings and knows to call soon. I can't say what they mean—that's for the nurse. Anything else while you wait?"

**Patient:** "no. just hoping they call soon"

**Agent:** "They will. Thanks for your patience."

theme: asks how long a nurse will take to call back, frustrated after 30 hours
